section_1.title: The Classical Search Dilemma
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of searching an unsorted database. Explain the limitations of classical computing (Linear Search) where you have to check every item one by one.
section_1.example: Imagine a mischievous cat named 'Pixel' hiding in one of 100 identical cardboard boxes. In a classical world, you'd have to open 50 boxes on average to find Pixel. If there are N boxes, it takes O(N) time.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Quantum Canvas
section_2.content: Briefly introduce Superposition. Explain that in quantum computing, we don't look at boxes one by one; we look at a 'superposition' of all boxes simultaneously.
section_2.example: Visual: Represent 4 boxes as 4 vertical bars of equal height (amplitudes). At the start, the probability of Pixel being in any box is equal. Math visual: |ψ⟩ = 1/√N Σ |i⟩.

section_3.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
section_3.content: Introduce the 'Oracle' as a black box that can recognize the target. The Oracle doesn't reveal the location but 'marks' it by flipping its phase (turning its amplitude upside down).
section_3.example: Visual: All bars remain positive except for the 'Pixel' box, which flips below the horizontal axis. It’s like a reflection across the 0-line. The state becomes negative, but the probability (magnitude squared) remains the same.

section_4.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
section_4.content: This is the 'magic' step. Explain the mathematical trick of reflecting all amplitudes around the average (mean) value of all states. This boosts the target's height while shrinking the others.
section_4.example: Visual: Draw a dashed line representing the 'Average Height' of all bars. Because one bar is negative, the average is slightly lower than the others. When we flip all bars over this dashed line, the 'Pixel' bar shoots up high above the rest, while the others drop near zero.

section_5.title: Iteration and Measurement
section_5.content: Explain that one flip isn't always enough. We repeat Steps 1 and 2 (the Grover Iteration) approximately √N times to maximize the target's amplitude before measuring.
section_5.example: Visual: An animation showing the target bar growing taller and the 'noise' bars getting smaller with each pulse. Warning: If you repeat too many times, the amplitude starts to decrease again (like over-rotating a dial).

section_6.title: The Quantum Speedup Summary
section_6.content: Conclude with the efficiency of the algorithm. Compare O(N) classical vs O(√N) quantum. Highlight that for 1 million items, classical takes 500,000 tries, but Grover takes only 1,000.
section_6.example: Final Visual: A split screen. On the left, a classical robot is exhausted opening 100 boxes. On the right, a quantum computer identifies Pixel in just 10 'pulses'. Quadratic speedup achieved!

- **Section 4 (Key):** Animates the "Inversion about the Mean" to boost the target.
- **Section 5 (Key):** Illustrates the iterative nature of the algorithm and final measurement.
- **Section 6:** Compares classical O(N) vs. quantum O(√N) efficiency.

animations: Show 4 vertical bars (#00FF00) representing boxes, with labels '00', '01', '10', '11'.
Make all bars equal height, with the formula '1/√N Σ |i⟩' (#FFFFFF) appearing above.
Add a soft glow effect (#ADD8E6) to all bars to represent 'Quantum Superposition'.

section_3.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
lecture_lines: We start with four bars, labeling one as our target.
The Oracle flips the target amplitude below the axis.
This pulsing yellow border highlights the marked state.
This process is known as a phase inversion.
The target's probability magnitude remains the same.
animations: Show the 4 bars from the previous section. Label the '10' bar as 'Target' (#FFFF00).
The 'Target' bar flips below the horizontal x-axis, becoming a negative amplitude.
Highlight the flipped 'Target' bar with a pulsing yellow (#FFFF00) border.
Show the label 'Phase Inversion' (#FFFFFF) next to the flipped bar.
Display the text: 'Probability |a|^2 remains unchanged' (#ADD8E6) near the flipped bar.

section_4.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
lecture_lines: Next, we reflect all amplitudes around their average value.
This "inversion about the mean" is a mathematical trick.
The average is slightly lowered by the negative target amplitude.
Reflecting makes the target amplitude much larger than the others.
Other amplitudes shrink, boosting our chance of finding the target.
animations: Show the bars (one negative, three positive) and a horizontal dashed white (#FFFFFF) line for 'Mean'.
Shift the 'Mean' line down slightly to reflect the average of all current amplitudes.
Reflect all bars across the dashed 'Mean' line: the target bar shoots up, others shrink.
Highlight the now-tall target bar with a bright yellow (#FFFF00) glow.
Display the text 'Inversion About the Mean' (#FFFFFF) at the top of the screen.

section_5.title: Iteration and Measurement
lecture_lines: We loop the Oracle and Diffusion steps together.
With each iteration, the target amplitude grows much taller.
We repeat this process roughly square root of N times.
Finally, we measure the system to collapse the state.
The algorithm successfully finds the target with high probability.
animations: Show a green (#00FF00) loop icon around symbols for 'Oracle' and 'Diffusion'.
Animate the bars again: the target bar grows taller while the others shrink further.
Display the text 'Repeat approximately √N times' (#ADD8E6) at the bottom.
Simulate a measurement: the tall target bar is selected, and all other bars disappear.
Show the text 'Target Found!' in bright green (#00FF00) with a flashing effect.

section_6.title: The Quantum Speedup Summary
lecture_lines: Grover's algorithm provides a significant quadratic speedup over classical.
A million items take only one thousand quantum iterations.
Quantum mechanics finds the needle in the haystack much faster.
animations: Display a split-screen comparison: 'Classical: O(N)' on left, 'Grover: O(√N)' on right.
Show a counter: 1,000,000 steps (Classical) vs 1,000 steps (Grover) (#ADD8E6).
Display the text 'Quadratic Speedup Achieved!' in gold (#FFD700) with a flash effect.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Iteration and Measurement"
        lines = [
            "We loop the Oracle and Diffusion steps together.",
            "With each iteration, the target amplitude grows much taller.",
            "We repeat this process roughly square root of N times.",
            "Finally, we measure the system to collapse the state.",
            "The algorithm successfully finds the target with high probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a green (#00FF00) loop icon around symbols for 'Oracle' and 'Diffusion'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        oracle_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=BLUE_B).set_fill(BLUE_E, opacity=0.3)
        oracle_text = MathTex("Oracle", color=WHITE)
        oracle_group = VGroup(oracle_box, oracle_text)
        self.place_at_grid(oracle_group, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        diffusion_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=ORANGE).set_fill(DARK_BROWN, opacity=0.3)
        diffusion_text = MathTex("Diffusion", color=WHITE)
        diffusion_group = VGroup(diffusion_box, diffusion_text)
        self.place_at_grid(diffusion_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Loop arrow
        loop_arrow = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B5"] + UP*0.5, self.grid["B2"] + UP*0.5, angle=-TAU/3, color="#00FF00")
        loop_arrow_back = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B2"] + DOWN*0.5, self.grid["B5"] + DOWN*0.5, angle=-TAU/3, color="#00FF00")
        loop_group = VGroup(loop_arrow, loop_arrow_back)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(oracle_group), FadeIn(diffusion_group))
        self.play(Create(loop_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate the bars again: the target bar grows taller while the others shrink further.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create bars
        bar_colors = [GRAY, GRAY, GREEN, GRAY]
        bar_heights_start = [0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.4]
        bar_heights_end = [0.1, 0.1, 2.0, 0.1]
        
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.4, height=h, color=c, fill_opacity=0.8) 
            for h, c in zip(bar_heights_start, bar_colors)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.place_in_area(bars, "C2", "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Move symbols up to make room
        self.play(
            oracle_group.animate.shift(UP * 0.5).scale(0.8),
            diffusion_group.animate.shift(UP * 0.5).scale(0.8),
            loop_group.animate.shift(UP * 0.5).scale(0.8),
            FadeIn(bars)
        )
        
        # Animate bars growing/shrinking
        animations = []
        for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
            target_h = bar_heights_end[i]
            # Use Scale in Y to avoid translation issues if center is used
            # But better to just replace the heights manually to keep alignment
            new_bar = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=target_h, color=bar.color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            new_bar.move_to(bar.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            animations.append(Transform(bar, new_bar))
            
        self.play(*animations, run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the text 'Repeat approximately √N times' (#ADD8E6) at the bottom.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        repeat_text = MathTex(r"\text{Repeat approximately } \sqrt{N} \text{ times}", color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_in_area(repeat_text, "E2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(repeat_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Simulate a measurement: the tall target bar is selected, and all other bars disappear.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Target bar index is 2
        noise_bars = VGroup(bars[0], bars[1], bars[3])
        target_bar = bars[2]
        
        # Pulse effect on target bar
        self.play(
            FadeOut(noise_bars),
            FadeOut(oracle_group),
            FadeOut(diffusion_group),
            FadeOut(loop_group),
            FadeOut(repeat_text),
            target_bar.animate.set_color(YELLOW).scale(1.1)
        )
        
        # Show collapse effect
        collapse_line = Line(target_bar.get_bottom() + LEFT*1.5, target_bar.get_bottom() + RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(collapse_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Show the text 'Target Found!' in bright green (#00FF00) with a flashing effect.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        found_text = Text("Target Found!", color="#00FF00", font_size=40)
        self.place_in_area(found_text, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(found_text))
        
        # Flashing effect
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(found_text.animate.set_opacity(0.3), run_time=0.2)
            self.play(found_text.animate.set_opacity(1.0), run_time=0.2)
            
        self.wait(2)

            Rectangle(width=0.7, height=2.2, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=glow_color, stroke_width=0)

            Write(formula),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: "This state is the starting point for Grover's algorithm."
        # Step 3: Add a soft glow effect (#ADD8E6) to all bars to represent 'Quantum Superposition'.
        
        # Update glow positions in case bars moved (though they stayed in center of grid cells)
        for i in range(4):
            glows[i].move_to(bars[i].get_center())

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            FadeIn(glows, scale=1.2),
            bars.animate.set_stroke(glow_color, opacity=0.8),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset final line color
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

            "A million items take only one thousand quantum iterations.",
            "Quantum mechanics finds the needle in the haystack much faster."
        ]

            MathTex(r"O(\sqrt{N})", font_size=36, color=line1_color)

        self.place_in_area(grover_label, "B5", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)

            classical_val.get_value(),
            num_decimal_places=0,

            font_size=32,

        ).add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(classical_val.get_value()))

        grover_group = VGroup(grover_counter, grover_unit).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(classical_group, "D2", "E3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(grover_group, "D5", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.add(classical_group, grover_group)
        
        # Animate counting
        # Classical counts to 1,000,000 while Grover counts to 1,000
        self.play(
            classical_val.animate.set_value(1000000),
            grover_val.animate.set_value(1000),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the text 'Quadratic Speedup Achieved!' in gold (#FFD700) with a flash effect.
        line3_color = "#FFD700"
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(line3_color)
        
        speedup_text = Text("Quadratic Speedup Achieved!", font_size=32, color=line3_color)
        # L017: Distribute visuals; L008: Centering horizontally across the whole right area
        self.place_in_area(speedup_text, "F2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Flash effect
        flash = Flash(speedup_text, color=line3_color, line_length=0.3, num_lines=12, flash_radius=2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(speedup_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(flash)
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Iteration and Measurement"
        lines = [
            "We loop the Oracle and Diffusion steps together.",
            "With each iteration, the target amplitude grows much taller.",
            "We repeat this process roughly square root of N times.",
            "Finally, we measure the system to collapse the state.",
            "The algorithm successfully finds the target with high probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        oracle_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=BLUE_B).set_fill(BLUE_E, opacity=0.3)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        oracle_text = Text("Oracle", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        oracle_group = VGroup(oracle_box, oracle_text)
        self.place_at_grid(oracle_group, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        diffusion_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=ORANGE).set_fill(DARK_BROWN, opacity=0.3)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        diffusion_text = Text("Diffusion", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        diffusion_group = VGroup(diffusion_box, diffusion_text)
        self.place_at_grid(diffusion_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Loop arrow
        # Create arrows manually relative to grid points
        loop_arrow = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B5"] + UP*0.4, self.grid["B2"] + UP*0.4, angle=-TAU/4, color="#00FF00")
        loop_arrow_back = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B2"] + DOWN*0.4, self.grid["B5"] + DOWN*0.4, angle=-TAU/4, color="#00FF00")
        loop_group = VGroup(loop_arrow, loop_arrow_back)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(oracle_group), FadeIn(diffusion_group))
        self.play(Create(loop_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        bar_colors = [GRAY, GRAY, GREEN, GRAY]
        bar_heights_start = [0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.4]
        bar_heights_end = [0.1, 0.1, 2.0, 0.1]
        
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.4, height=h, color=c, fill_opacity=0.8) 
            for h, c in zip(bar_heights_start, bar_colors)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "C2", "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Move symbols to Row A to make room
        new_oracle = VGroup(oracle_box.copy(), oracle_text.copy())
        self.place_at_grid(new_oracle, "A2", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        new_diffusion = VGroup(diffusion_box.copy(), diffusion_text.copy())
        self.place_at_grid(new_diffusion, "A5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        new_loop = loop_group.copy()
        # Scale and move loop relative to new positions
        new_loop.scale(0.8).move_to((self.grid["A2"] + self.grid["A5"])/2)

        self.play(
            Transform(oracle_group, new_oracle),
            Transform(diffusion_group, new_diffusion),
            Transform(loop_group, new_loop),
            FadeIn(bars)
        )
        
        # Animate bars
        # We'll use scaling about the bottom edge to avoid move_to
        self.play(
            *[bars[i].animate.stretch_to_fit_height(bar_heights_end[i], about_edge=DOWN) for i in range(4)],
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        repeat_text = Text("Repeat approximately √N times", color="#ADD8E6", font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(repeat_text, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(repeat_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        noise_bars = VGroup(bars[0], bars[1], bars[3])
        target_bar = bars[2]
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(noise_bars),
            FadeOut(oracle_group),
            FadeOut(diffusion_group),
            FadeOut(loop_group),
            FadeOut(repeat_text),
            target_bar.animate.set_color(YELLOW).scale(1.2)
        )
        
        # Collapse line at the base of the bar
        base_y = target_bar.get_bottom()[1]
        center_x = target_bar.get_center()[0]
        collapse_line = Line(np.array([center_x - 1.5, base_y, 0]), np.array([center_x + 1.5, base_y, 0]), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(collapse_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        found_text = Text("Target Found!", color="#00FF00", font_size=40)
        self.place_in_area(found_text, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(found_text))
        
        # Flashing effect
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(found_text.animate.set_opacity(0.3), run_time=0.2)
            self.play(found_text.animate.set_opacity(1.0), run_time=0.2)
            
        self.wait(2)

lecture_lines: Next, we reflect all amplitudes around their average value.
This "inversion about the mean" is a mathematical trick.
The average is slightly lowered by the negative target amplitude.
Reflecting makes the target amplitude much larger than the others.
Other amplitudes shrink, boosting our chance of finding the target.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Next, we reflect all amplitudes around their average value.",
            "This \"inversion about the mean\" is a mathematical trick.",
            "The average is slightly lowered by the negative target amplitude.",
            "Reflecting makes the target amplitude much larger than the others.",
            "Other amplitudes shrink, boosting our chance of finding the target."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        BLUE_B = "#58C4DD"
        RED_B = "#F44336"
        MEAN_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        
        # Grid positions for bars
        bar_cols = ["2", "3", "4", "5"]
        baseline_y = self.grid["D1"][1]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the bars (one negative, three positive) and a horizontal dashed white (#FFFFFF) line for 'Mean'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        bars = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            # Initial heights: positive states and the flipped target state from the oracle
            h = 0.6 if i < 3 else -0.6
            color = BLUE_B if i < 3 else RED_B
            bar = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=abs(h), fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=color, stroke_width=2)
            pos = self.grid[f"D{bar_cols[i]}"]
            if h > 0:
                bar.move_to(pos + UP * (bar.height / 2))
            else:
                bar.move_to(pos + DOWN * (bar.height / 2))
            bars.add(bar)
            
        # Initial Mean line at 0.6 (level of the 3 positive bars)
        mean_line_y = baseline_y + 0.6
        mean_line = DashedLine(
            start=[self.grid["D2"][0] - 0.4, mean_line_y, 0],
            end=[self.grid["D5"][0] + 0.4, mean_line_y, 0],
            color=MEAN_COLOR
        )
        mean_label = Text("Mean", font_size=18, color=MEAN_COLOR)
        # Position label near the line in Row C
        self.place_at_grid(mean_label, "C1")
        mean_label.next_to(mean_line, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(bars), Create(mean_line), Write(mean_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Shift the 'Mean' line down slightly to reflect the average of all current amplitudes.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculated new mean: (0.6 + 0.6 + 0.6 - 0.6) / 4 = 1.2 / 4 = 0.3
        new_mean_y = baseline_y + 0.3
        self.play(
            mean_line.animate.move_to([mean_line.get_center()[0], new_mean_y, 0]),
            mean_label.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reflect all bars across the dashed 'Mean' line: the target bar shoots up, others shrink.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Reflection formula: x_new = 2*mean - x_old
        # Positive bars: 2*0.3 - 0.6 = 0.0
        # Negative bar: 2*0.3 - (-0.6) = 1.2
        target_heights = [0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 1.2]
        
        transforms = []
        for i in range(4):
            new_h = target_heights[i]
            # Maintain bar width and color
            target_rect = Rectangle(width=0.5, height=new_h, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=bars[i].fill_color, stroke_width=2)
            # All bars are now positive or near-zero, so we move them UP from baseline
            target_rect.move_to(self.grid[f"D{bar_cols[i]}"] + UP * (target_rect.height / 2))
            transforms.append(Transform(bars[i], target_rect))
            
        self.play(*transforms)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight the now-tall target bar with a bright yellow (#FFFF00) glow.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a glow effect around the target bar
        glow = bars[3].copy().set_fill(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, opacity=0.3).scale(1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(Indicate(bars[3], color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, scale_factor=1.05))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Display the text 'Inversion About the Mean' (#FFFFFF) at the top of the screen.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        inversion_text = Text("Inversion About the Mean", font_size=28, color=WHITE)
        # Position centered in the top of the chart area (Row B)
        self.place_in_area(inversion_text, "B2", "B5")
        
        self.play(Write(inversion_text), FadeOut(glow))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from shared state
        title = "The Quantum Speedup Summary"
        lines = [
            "Grover's algorithm provides a significant quadratic speedup over classical.",
            "A million items take only one thousand quantum iterations.",
            "Quantum mechanics finds the needle in the haystack much faster."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a split-screen comparison: 'Classical: O(N)' on left, 'Grover: O(√N)' on right.
        line1_color = BLUE_A
        self.lecture[0].set_color(line1_color)
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        classical_label = VGroup(
            Text("Classical:", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("O(N)", font_size=36, color=line1_color)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        grover_label = VGroup(
            Text("Grover:", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            # Use unicode square root symbol
            Text("O(√N)", font_size=36, color=line1_color)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        # L008: Using place_in_area to balance visuals
        self.place_in_area(classical_label, "B2", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(grover_label, "B5", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Visual separator
        separator = Line(self.grid["B4"] + UP*0.5, self.grid["E4"] + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY_E)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(classical_label),
            FadeIn(grover_label),
            Create(separator),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a counter using Text and updaters to avoid DecimalNumber (which requires LaTeX)
        line2_color = "#ADD8E6"
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(line2_color)
        
        # Value trackers for the counter effect
        classical_val = ValueTracker(1)
        grover_val = ValueTracker(1)
        
        # Manually create counting numbers using Text to avoid 'latex' error
        classical_counter = Text("1", font_size=32, color=line2_color)
        classical_counter.add_updater(
            lambda d: d.become(
                Text(f"{int(classical_val.get_value()):,}", font_size=32, color=line2_color)
                .move_to(d.get_center())
            )
        )
        
        grover_counter = Text("1", font_size=32, color=line2_color)

        self.add(classical_group, grover_group)
        
        # Animate counting
        self.play(
            classical_val.animate.set_value(1000000),
            grover_val.animate.set_value(1000),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the text 'Quadratic Speedup Achieved!' in gold (#FFD700) with a flash effect.
        line3_color = "#FFD700"
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(line3_color)
        
        speedup_text = Text("Quadratic Speedup Achieved!", font_size=32, color=line3_color)
        # Distribute visuals across the bottom right area
        self.place_in_area(speedup_text, "F2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Flash effect
        flash = Flash(speedup_text, color=line3_color, line_length=0.3, num_lines=12, flash_radius=2)
        
        self.play(
            Write(speedup_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(flash)
        self.wait(3)

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from shared state
        title = "The Quantum Speedup Summary"
        lines = [
            "Grover's algorithm provides a significant quadratic speedup over classical.",
            "A million items take only one thousand quantum iterations.",
            "Quantum mechanics finds the needle in the haystack much faster."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a split-screen comparison: 'Classical: O(N)' on left, 'Grover: O(√N)' on right.
        line1_color = BLUE_A
        self.lecture[0].set_color(line1_color)
        
        # Assets: Haystack icon

        self.place_at_grid(haystack, "A4", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        classical_label = VGroup(
            Text("Classical:", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            Text("O(N)", font_size=36, color=line1_color)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        grover_label = VGroup(
            Text("Grover:", font_size=24, color=WHITE),
            # Use unicode square root symbol
            Text("O(√N)", font_size=36, color=line1_color)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        # L008: Using place_in_area to balance visuals
        # Addressing Issue 38: Move to Row A-B
        self.place_in_area(classical_label, "A2", "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(grover_label, "A5", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Visual separator
        separator = Line(self.grid["A4"] + DOWN*0.2, self.grid["F4"] + DOWN*0.5, color=GREY_E)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(haystack),
            FadeIn(classical_label),
            FadeIn(grover_label),
            Create(separator),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a counter using DecimalNumber (standard Manim, num_decimal_places=0 for integer effect)
        line2_color = "#ADD8E6"
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(line2_color)
        
        # Value trackers for the counter effect
        classical_val = ValueTracker(1)
        grover_val = ValueTracker(1)
        
        # Use DecimalNumber for performance (avoids Text reconstruction)
        classical_counter = DecimalNumber(1, num_decimal_places=0, group_with_commas=True, font_size=32, color=line2_color)

        classical_group = VGroup(classical_counter, classical_unit).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        grover_group = VGroup(grover_counter, grover_unit).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Addressing Issue 39: Positioning C2-D3 and C5-D6 with scale 0.8
        self.place_in_area(classical_group, "C2", "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(grover_group, "C5", "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.add(classical_group, grover_group)
        
        # Animate counting
        self.play(
            classical_val.animate.set_value(1000000),
            grover_val.animate.set_value(1000),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display the text 'Quadratic Speedup Achieved!' in gold (#FFD700) alongside needle icon

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(line3_color)
        
        # Assets: Needle icon
        needle = SVGMobject("/mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/needle.svg")

        speedup_text = Text("Quadratic Speedup Achieved!", font_size=32, color=line3_color)
        # Addressing Issue 40: Positioning E2-F6 with scale 0.7
        self.place_in_area(speedup_text, "E2", "F6", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Flash effect
        flash = Flash(speedup_text, color=line3_color, line_length=0.3, num_lines=12, flash_radius=2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(needle),
            Write(speedup_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(flash)
        self.wait(3)
